why: The answer says public static void main() works as an entry point because the program uses no arguments, but Java requires the header public static void main(String[] args), so java Hello cannot launch the class without it.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine because the program uses no arguments.
concepts.why: This is the MainWithoutStringArgs wrong rule: java needs the main(String[] args) header to start the program, whether or not the program reads any arguments.
The answer mentions arguments only to excuse leaving out the parameter, and makes no claim about how args works.
